steps.what: Select appropriate approved flyers or brochures and distribute them to community members

tasks.design: Keep physical distribution and practical explanation with the worker. Approved originals remain in {DOCS}; this task does not add content creation or assume recipients can use digital delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reaching people can require physical presence and the right language or format.
tasks.enabler_now: Document generation does not hand materials to community members.
tasks.still_hard: Literacy, language and trust affect whether materials are understood.
tasks.human_edge: The worker notices who needs explanation or a different format.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in distribution effort or content-approval authority.

evidence.claim: Physical distribution remains human work; neither document authoring nor digital recipient access is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is selecting from approved stock and distributing it, excluding authoring, design and print production.
Health education staff supply existing approved materials upstream with unchanged effort. No machine step requires structured recipients or language flags.
No implementation or additional upkeep is introduced, so incremental hours are zero.
unknowns: Distribution channels and recipients' format needs
research_questions: Which recipients need personal explanation alongside printed information?

already_counted.description: All material selection and physical distribution

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 and zero upkeep; unchanged physical distribution yields zero saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Identify and contact people for targeted outreach

steps.what: Identify appropriate outreach contacts through permitted referrals and knowledge of the community
Contact members of targeted groups respectfully and explain the available support

tasks.design: Retain contact identification and personal outreach with the worker. Existing authorised referral information may remain in {DOCS}; no inferred risk labels or automated targeting are introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Appropriate contact depends on trust, purpose and permission.
tasks.enabler_now: A case-note tool does not determine who should receive outreach.
tasks.still_hard: An unwanted contact may expose sensitive circumstances or undermine trust.
tasks.human_edge: The worker recognises respectful ways to approach people and accepts refusal.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in outreach effort or authority to use personal information.

evidence.claim: Targeted outreach is retained as contextual identification and human contact; no structured high-risk list or automated targeting capability is presumed.

assumptions: Boundary is the worker's identification and contact activity, excluding clinical risk assessment and programme eligibility.

Referral partners produce existing permitted referrals upstream with unchanged effort; the worker checks appropriateness within retained s1. No free pregnancy, income or minority-status dataset is assumed.
No implementation or additional upkeep is proposed; incremental hours are zero.
unknowns: Permitted referral sources and outreach rules
research_questions: Which contact approaches do community members regard as appropriate?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 with zero upkeep. Identification and direct outreach remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Advise clients or groups about sanitation and hygiene and check practical understanding

tasks.design: Keep hygiene explanation, demonstration where needed and understanding checks with the worker. Use existing approved guidance in {DOCS}; no new content drafting or shorter interaction is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advice must fit people's understanding and practical circumstances.
tasks.enabler_now: Information availability does not establish that a practice can be followed.
tasks.still_hard: Resources, habits and language can prevent adoption.
tasks.human_edge: The worker explains without judgement and checks what is practical.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in hygiene-advice effort or professional boundaries.

evidence.claim: Hygiene advice remains a personal explanation and understanding check; no report-writing baseline is added.

assumptions: Boundary is advice and practical explanation, excluding developing public-health guidance.
Health educators supply existing approved guidance upstream with unchanged effort. Client circumstances are clarified during retained s1; no machine step needs structured fields.
No implementation or new upkeep is proposed; incremental effort is zero.
research_questions: Can clients demonstrate the practice after the explanation?

already_counted.description: All hygiene explanation and understanding checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 and zero upkeep; unchanged personal explanation yields zero saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Advise clients or community groups about diagnostic screenings using approved programme information

tasks.design: Retain the worker's screening explanation and response to questions. Existing approved information in {DOCS} supports the discussion; clinicians and screening programmes retain individual eligibility and clinical decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: People need clear explanations and help recognising the right contact.
tasks.enabler_now: Case-note drafting does not answer individual screening concerns reliably.
tasks.still_hard: Questions may require clinical interpretation outside the worker's role.
tasks.human_edge: The worker notices misunderstanding, explains boundaries and supports appropriate follow-up.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in screening-advice effort or clinical authority.

evidence.claim: Screening explanation is retained as human guidance; the task does not establish a separate eligibility-calculation or document-production workload.

assumptions: Boundary is explanation and navigation, excluding tests, results interpretation, diagnosis and individual eligibility decisions.
Screening programmes produce existing approved information upstream with unchanged effort. Client questions are clarified inside retained s1; no structured eligibility flag is assumed.
No new tool or upkeep is introduced; incremental hours are zero.
unknowns: Approved screening materials and referral routes
research_questions: Which questions must be referred to the screening programme or clinician?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 and zero upkeep; unchanged explanation and navigation yields zero saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

reach: Support health educators with accessible explanations
Coordinate respectful referrals with service assistants
role.ambitious_version: A community worker who reaches people respectfully and helps them understand approved information and appropriate next contacts.
